name: manual_bb27e0
claim: When a fast-forward sync is blocked by a local uncommitted change of unknown provenance (not authored this session), git stash it with a descriptive message rather than discarding it or guessing whether to keep it -- preserves the work for later review without blocking the sync or silently destroying something intentional.

decisions.notes: A local .codex/config.toml diff (bash-wrapper exa MCP vs npx mcp-remote) blocked a 22-commit fast-forward. Comparing the stashed version to the newly-synced upstream version showed upstream had deliberately kept the more robust bash-resolver approach -- reapplying the stash would have been a regression, but discarding it outright would have destroyed someone else's work without knowing why it existed.
